title: Acids and Bases
seo_title: Grade 10 Science (SNC2D): Acids and Bases Worksheets (Ontario)
standard_text: The properties of acids and bases; the pH scale and indicators; neutralization; reactions of acids with metals and carbonates; and acids and bases in the environment, including acid precipitation. (summary of The Ontario Curriculum, Grades 9 and 10: Science (2008), Science, Grade 10, Academic (SNC2D), Strand C: Chemical Reactions)
meta_desc: Free Grade 10 Science (SNC2D) worksheets on acids and bases: properties, the pH scale, indicators, neutralization, salts, reactions with metals and carbonates, and acid rain. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: pH below 7 is acidic, 7 is neutral, above 7 is basic.
body_html:
How to think about it

Acids taste sour, turn blue litmus red and react with many metals to give hydrogen gas. Bases taste bitter, feel slippery and turn red litmus blue. The pH scale runs from 0 to 14; each step is a tenfold change in acidity.

In neutralization, an acid and a base react to form a salt and water (HCl + NaOH → NaCl + H₂O). Acids react with carbonates to give a salt, water and carbon dioxide. Sulfur dioxide and nitrogen oxides from burning fuels form acid precipitation, which harms lakes, forests and buildings; limestone neutralizes it.

Example

Products of HCl + KOH?

Acid + base → salt + water

Answer: KCl and H₂O

Example

A lake goes from pH 6 to pH 5. How much more acidic is it?

One pH step = ×10

Answer: 10 times

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a pH of 6 is ten times less acidic than pH 5 but calling it basic.
  • Saying all salts are sodium chloride.
  • Thinking a strong acid and a concentrated acid are the same.

items.q: CO₂ dissolves in seawater and forms carbonic acid. What happens to ocean pH?
c: It goes down (the water becomes more acidic).
items.e: More H⁺ ions → lower pH. Since 1750, surface ocean pH fell from about 8.2 to 8.1.

items.q: Why are lakes on the Canadian Shield easily harmed by acid rain?
